column42: This one seems to be an older female. I heard her howling before I saw her trotting past up the estate road. In a couple of these photos she was giving voice as I took the photos. There USED to be a LOT of wallabies - swamp wallabies and whiptails and red-necked wallabies - hanging around this area, 2015-2019. We used to holiday there regularly, every year or two years; then not in 2020, 2021 or 2022; this year is first time we've been back; first thing we noticed was a LOT fewer wallabies... and then we observed dingoes in the area (both heard and seen). Note: pet dogs are not permitted in this estate which immediately adjoins national park. A further thought is that if a pair or family of dingoes have established themselves within the national park, this may help suppress any fox or feral cat activity; and may also - in time - help with control of the feral pigs (I don't know whether dingoes are prepared to take down adult pigs but surely they would be capable of grabbing a piglet or two or three!).

Dingos are vulnerable-their identity subverted to ‘wild dogs’ to enable agricultural industry and government sanctioned culling. Theyre going extinct yet theyre the best thing for our environment as top predators keeping the tropic balance in check.
